# Textbooks & Course Literature

This repository references several classic and foundational textbooks for mathematical methods, classical mechanics, and general physics.

## Core Mechanics

### Classical Mechanics (2005)
**Author:** John R. Taylor
**Publisher:** University Science Books
**Description:** The primary textbook for PHYC54H3. Known for its conversational tone and extreme clarity, it builds from elementary Newtonian mechanics to advanced topics like the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formalisms, central-force motion, and chaos theory.
**Link:** [University Science Books - Taylor](https://uscibooks.aip.org/books/classical-mechanics/)

### Introduction to Classical Mechanics: With Problems and Solutions (2008)
**Author:** David Morin
**Publisher:** Cambridge University Press
**Description:** Highly regarded for its vast collection of very challenging problems, making it a staple for physics Olympiad preparation. The textbook emphasizes clever problem-solving techniques and covers the Lagrangian method extensively.
**Link:** [Cambridge University Press - Morin](https://www.cambridge.org/highereducation/books/introduction-to-classical-mechanics/30AD597A8D8ED7FAD5C5F1CBEEF4EDC6#overview)

### The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Volume I: Mainly Mechanics, Radiation, and Heat
**Authors:** Richard P. Feynman, Robert B. Leighton, and Matthew Sands
**Publisher:** Basic Books (Online edition by Caltech)
**Description:** The legendary lecture series by Nobel laureate Richard Feynman. It approaches classical mechanics with unmatched physical intuition, emphasizing deep conceptual understanding over rote mathematics.
**Link:** [Feynman Lectures Vol. I](https://www.feynmanlectures.caltech.edu/I_toc.html)

### Mechanics (Course of Theoretical Physics, Volume 1)
**Authors:** L. D. Landau and E. M. Lifshitz
**Publisher:** Elsevier (Butterworth-Heinemann)
**Description:** A hallmark of Russian theoretical physics, this dense and mathematically elegant text begins directly with the principle of least action and develops the entirety of mechanics deductively. Ideal for advanced students.
**Link:** [Elsevier - Landau & Lifshitz](https://www.elsevier.com/books/mechanics/landau/978-0-7506-2896-9)

### Mathematical Methods of Classical Mechanics (Graduate Texts in Mathematics, Vol. 60)
**Author:** V. I. Arnold
**Publisher:** Springer
**Description:** A classic graduate-level textbook that provides a modern, geometric approach to classical mechanics. It builds mechanics from the ground up using the geometry of manifolds, symplectic geometry, and Lie groups.
**Link:** [Springer - Arnold](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4757-2063-1)

## Mathematical Methods

### Mathematical Methods for Physics and Engineering
**Authors:** K. F. Riley, M. P. Hobson, and S. J. Bence
**Publisher:** Cambridge University Press
**Description:** An immensely practical guide covering all undergraduate mathematical requirements, from basic calculus and vectors to complex variables, tensors, and group theory.
**Link:** [Cambridge University Press - Riley](https://www.cambridge.org/highereducation/books/mathematical-methods-for-physics-and-engineering/1DEBEED7643BA46AD4ED5E4FE3487013#overview)

### Mathematical Methods for Physicists
**Authors:** George B. Arfken and Hans J. Weber
**Publisher:** Academic Press (Elsevier)
**Description:** Known as the "bible" of mathematical physics, this comprehensive text goes extremely deep into vector analysis, differential equations, and special functions.
**Link:** [Elsevier - Arfken](https://www.elsevier.com/books/mathematical-methods-for-physicists/arfken/978-0-12-384654-9)

### Mathematical Methods in the Physical Sciences
**Author:** Mary L. Boas
**Publisher:** John Wiley & Sons
**Description:** An approachable but rigorous text that bridges the gap between basic calculus and the advanced mathematics required in upper-level physics courses.
**Link:** [Wiley - Boas](https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Mathematical+Methods+in+the+Physical+Sciences%2C+3rd+Edition-p-9780471198260)

---

## General Physics

### Physics, Volume 1 (5th Edition)
**Authors:** Robert Resnick, David Halliday, Kenneth S. Krane
**Publisher:** John Wiley & Sons
**Description:** The definitive introductory calculus-based physics text. This classical tome is incredibly thorough on mechanics, thermodynamics, and waves.
**Link:** [Wiley - Krane](https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Physics%2C+Volume+1%2C+5th+Edition-p-9780471320579)

# Online Open Courses

### MIT OCW 8.01SC Classical Mechanics (Fall 2016)
**Description:** A spectacular open courseware resource from MIT, emphasizing problem-solving and rigorous foundational mechanics. Contains lecture notes, problem sets, and video lectures.
**Link:** [MIT 8.01SC Classical Mechanics](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/8-01sc-classical-mechanics-fall-2016/)

### Fundamentals of Physics I (PHYS 200) - Open Yale Courses
**Instructor:** Prof. Ramamurti Shankar
**Description:** A complete, filmed introductory physics course covering Newtonian mechanics, special relativity, and thermodynamics. Shankar's lectures are famous for their engaging and insightful delivery.
**Link:** [Open Yale Courses - PHYS 200](https://oyc.yale.edu/physics/phys-200)

### MIT OCW 8.012 Physics I: Classical Mechanics (Fall 2008)
**Description:** An advanced version of the standard introductory mechanics course at MIT, aimed at students with strong math backgrounds. It explores Newtonian mechanics with greater rigor.
**Link:** [MIT 8.012 Classical Mechanics](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/8-012-physics-i-classical-mechanics-fall-2008/)

### MIT OCW 8.223 Classical Mechanics II (January IAP 2017)
**Description:** A fast-paced, intensive course focusing heavily on the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulations of classical mechanics, central forces, and rigid body dynamics.
**Link:** [MIT 8.223 Classical Mechanics II](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/8-223-classical-mechanics-ii-january-iap-2017/)

### MIT OCW 8.09 Classical Mechanics III (Fall 2014)
**Description:** An advanced undergraduate/graduate level course covering chaotic dynamics, canonical transformations, Hamilton-Jacobi theory, and continuum mechanics.
**Link:** [MIT 8.09 Classical Mechanics III](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/8-09-classical-mechanics-iii-fall-2014/)

# Computational References

### Python Programming and Numerical Methods: A Guide for Engineers and Scientists
**Authors:** Qingkai Kong, Timmy Siauw, Alexandre Bayen
**Description:** An open-access textbook (Jupyter Notebooks) from UC Berkeley detailing numerical Python (NumPy, SciPy) methods for ODEs, root finding, and basic data analysis.
**Link:** [Berkeley Python Numerical Methods](https://pythonnumericalmethods.studentorg.berkeley.edu/notebooks/Index.html)
